# SQLite

SQLite is a C-language library that implements a small, fast, self-contained, 
high-reliability, full-featured, SQL database engine. SQLite is the most used 
database engine in the world.

## What is SQLite?

SQLite is an embedded SQL database engine. Unlike most other SQL databases, 
SQLite does not have a separate server process. SQLite reads and writes 
directly to ordinary disk files. A complete SQL database with multiple tables, 
indices, triggers, and views, is contained in a single disk file.

## Where to Learn More

For comprehensive documentation about SQLite, including:
- How to use SQLite
- SQL syntax supported by SQLite
- Programming interfaces
- Performance characteristics
- Configuration options

Please visit the official SQLite website:

**[https://sqlite.org/](https://sqlite.org/)**

## Key Features

- **Serverless**: No separate server process required
- **Zero Configuration**: No setup or administration needed
- **Full-Featured**: Supports most of SQL92
- **Small Footprint**: Compact library, minimal memory usage
- **Reliable**: ACID transactions, even after system crashes
- **Cross-Platform**: Works on Unix, Windows, macOS, and many other systems

## License

SQLite is in the public domain. See [https://sqlite.org/copyright.html](https://sqlite.org/copyright.html) 
for details.

## Contact

- **Forum**: [https://sqlite.org/forum](https://sqlite.org/forum)
- **Website**: [https://sqlite.org/](https://sqlite.org/)
- **Security Issues**: drh at sqlite dot org

## Getting SQLite

Precompiled binaries and source code distributions are available at:

[https://sqlite.org/download.html](https://sqlite.org/download.html)
==========
License Information
===================

SQLite Is Public Domain
-----------------------

The SQLite source code, including all of the files in the directories
listed in the bullets below are 
[Public Domain](https://sqlite.org/copyright.html).
The authors have submitted written affidavits releasing their work to
the public for any use.  Every byte of the public-domain code can be
traced back to the original authors.  The files of this repository
that are public domain include the following:

  *  All of the primary SQLite source code files found in the
     [src/ directory](https://sqlite.org/src/tree/src?type=tree&expand)
  *  All of the test cases and testing code in the
     [test/ directory](https://sqlite.org/src/tree/test?type=tree&expand)
  *  All of the SQLite extension source code and test cases in the
     [ext/ directory](https://sqlite.org/src/tree/ext?type=tree&expand)
  *  All code that ends up in the "sqlite3.c" and "sqlite3.h" build products
     that actually implement the SQLite RDBMS.
  *  All of the code used to compile the
     [command-line interface](https://sqlite.org/cli.html)
  *  All of the code used to build various utility programs such as
     "sqldiff", "sqlite3_rsync", and "sqlite3_analyzer".


The public domain source files usually contain a header comment
similar to the following to make it clear that the software is
public domain.

> The author disclaims copyright to this source code.  In place of
> a legal notice, here is a blessing:
> 
>   *   May you do good and not evil.
>   *   May you find forgiveness for yourself and forgive others.
>   *   May you share freely, never taking more than you give.

Almost every file you find in this source repository will be
public domain.  But there are a small number of exceptions:

Non-Public-Domain Code Included With This Source Repository AS A Convenience
----------------------------------------------------------------------------

This repository contains a (relatively) small amount of non-public-domain
code used to help implement the configuration and build logic.  In other
words, there are some non-public-domain files used to implement:

> ./configure && make

In all cases, the non-public-domain files included with this
repository have generous BSD-style licenses.  So anyone is free to
use any of the code in this source repository for any purpose, though
attribution may be required to reuse or republish the configure and
build scripts.  None of the non-public-domain code ever actually reaches
the build products, such as "sqlite3.c", however, so no attribution is
required to use SQLite itself.  The non-public-domain code consists of
scripts used to help compile SQLite.  The non-public-domain code is
technically not part of SQLite.  The non-public-domain code is
included in this repository as a convenience to developers, so that those
who want to build SQLite do not need to go download a bunch of
third-party build scripts in order to compile SQLite.

Non-public-domain code included in this respository includes:

  *  The ["autosetup"](http://msteveb.github.io/autosetup/) configuration
     system that is contained (mostly) in the autosetup/ directory, but also
     includes the "./configure" script at the top-level of this archive.
     Autosetup has a separate BSD-style license.  See the
     [autosetup/LICENSE](http://msteveb.github.io/autosetup/license/)
     for details.

  *  There are BSD-style licenses on some of the configuration
     software found in the legacy autoconf/ directory and its
     subdirectories.

The following unix shell command can be run from the top-level
of this source repository in order to remove all non-public-domain
code:

> rm -rf configure autosetup autoconf

If you unpack this source repository and then run the command above, what
is left will be 100% public domain.

Structure of exec.c:
1. `Eval` context: Db, Arena, error, parameter bindings, current row context.
2. Name resolution: build a "scope" from a SrcList: for each source item, either a real table (columns) or a subquery (output columns). Provide `findColumn(scope, zTab, zCol)`.
3. Expression evaluation: `void evalExpr(Eval*, Expr*, Value*)`.
4. Aggregates: detect aggregate functions in the SELECT/WHERE etc. Since I'm doing a simple tree-walk executor, I'll handle aggregates by:
   - For each aggregate expression in the result list/HAVING/ORDER BY, evaluate it over the group rows.
   Implementation: `evalAggExpr(Eval*, Expr*, RowSet*, Value*)` which walks the expr tree and evaluates aggregates over the row set, non-aggregate parts using the first row of the group (sqlite allows bare columns in aggregates).
5. SELECT execution:
   - resolve
   - FROM: build row sources
   - WHERE filter
   - GROUP BY/aggregates
   - DISTINCT
   - ORDER BY
   - LIMIT/OFFSET
   - compound ops
6. DML: INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE with constraints and triggers.
7. DDL: CREATE/DROP/ALTER.

Data structures for "row sets": a list of Value arrays (one per output column) plus for joins the per-source columns.

Let me define:
```c
typedef struct RowBuf { Value **ap; int n, cap; int nCol; Arena *pA; } RowBuf;
```
Each row is a `Value*` array of nCol values.

For the join, I'll produce a flat row of all columns from all sources, with per-source column offsets.

Scope for resolution:
```c
typedef struct Scope {
  struct Src { char *zAlias; Table *pTab; int iStart, nCol; char **azCol; int *aiAff; Select *pSub; } a[32];
  int nSrc;
  Eval *pEv;
} Scope;
```
Where for a subquery source, azCol holds the subquery's output column names (resolved recursively).

- `EXPR TKX_COLUMN` with zTok2 (table qualifier) or NULL.

- Also handle special names: rowid/oid/_rowid_ → the rowid column.
- If not found: try outer scope (correlated subquery). I'll support a chain of scopes (parent pointer).

Let me implement `resolveExpr(Eval*, Expr*, Scope*)` that sets e->iSrc (source index) and e->iCol (column index within that source) or marks errors.

Then evaluation: `evalExpr` with a `CurRow` structure:

Actually simpler: I'll materialize the joined row as a single flat Value* array, and each source has an offset. For rowid, I'll keep a parallel array of rowids.

Let me define the "source" runtime:
```c

  Table *pTab;        /* 0 if subquery */

  char **azCol;       /* column names (from table or subquery) */
  int nCol;
  int *aiRowidIdx;    /* hmm */
} SrcRun;
```
For rowid access I need the rowid per row. I'll keep a parallel `i64 *aiRowid` for each source (for subqueries, rowid = the row index + 1).

- part A: Eval context, resolution, expression evaluation, functions (call into func.c).
- part B: SELECT execution.
- part C: DML/DDL.

And func.c for builtin functions.

Given the size, let me start with part A + part B in exec.c, and func.c.

- If a SELECT has aggregates or a GROUP BY, group the rows and evaluate per group.

static int grpFn(Eval *p, CurRow *cur, void *pArg){
  GrpCtx *gc = pArg;
  Value aKey[32];
  int i;
  int found = -1;
  if( gc->pWhere ){
    Value v;
    valInit(&v);
    evalExprIn(p, gc->pWhere, p->pScope, cur, &v);
    if( !evalIsTrue(&v) ) return 0;
  }
  for(i=0;i<gc->pGroupBy->nExpr;i++){
    valInit(&aKey[i]);
    evalExprIn(p, gc->pGroupBy->apExpr[i], p->pScope, cur, &aKey[i]);
  }
  for(i=0;i<gc->nGrp;i++){
    int j, ok = 1;
    for(j=0;j<gc->pGroupBy->nExpr;j++){
      if( valCmp(gc->apGrp[i].aKey+j, &aKey[j])!=0 ){ ok=0; break; }
    }
    if( ok ){ found = i; break; }
  }
  if( found<0 ){
    if( gc->nGrp>=gc->capGrp ){
      gc->capGrp = gc->capGrp?gc->capGrp*2:8;
      gc->apGrp = arenaRealloc(p->pA, gc->apGrp, gc->nGrp*sizeof(Grp), gc->capGrp*sizeof(Grp));
    }
    memset(&gc->apGrp[gc->nGrp],0,sizeof(Grp));
    gc->apGrp[gc->nGrp].aKey = arenaAlloc(p->pA, gc->pGroupBy->nExpr*sizeof(Value));
    for(i=0;i<gc->pGroupBy->nExpr;i++){ valInit(&gc->apGrp[gc->nGrp].aKey[i]); valCopy(p->pA,&gc->apGrp[gc->nGrp].aKey[i], &aKey[i]); }
    rowbufInit(&gc->apGrp[gc->nGrp].rows, p->pA, 0);
    found = gc->nGrp++;
  }
  rowbufAppend(&gc->apGrp[found].rows, cur->apFlat, 0);
  return 0;
}

static int buildInsertRow(Eval *p, Table *t, ExprList *pCols, ExprList *pRow, Value *aVal, int *pnOut){
  int i;
  int nCol = t->nCol;
  int aiMap[512];
  int nSpec = 0;
  for(i=0;i<nCol;i++) aiMap[i] = -1;
  if( pCols ){
    int j;
    nSpec = pCols->nExpr;
    for(j=0;j<nSpec;j++){
      int ic = colIndexOf(t, pCols->apExpr[j]->zTok);
      if( ic<0 ){
        errSetPos(p->pErr, pCols->apExpr[j]->start, "table %s has no column named %s", t->zName, pCols->apExpr[j]->zTok);
        return 1;
      }
      aiMap[ic] = j;
    }
  }else{
    int j;
    for(j=0;j<nCol;j++) aiMap[j] = j;
  }
  for(i=0;i<nCol;i++) valInit(&aVal[i]);
  for(i=0;i<nCol;i++){
    if( aiMap[i]>=0 ){
      if( aiMap[i] < (pRow?pRow->nExpr:0) ){
        valFromExpr(p, pRow->apExpr[aiMap[i]], &aVal[i]);
      }else{
        valSetNull(&aVal[i]);
      }
    }else if( t->aCol[i].zDflt ){
      /* default value */
      const char *z = t->aCol[i].zDflt;
      if( strEq(z,"NULL") ) valSetNull(&aVal[i]);
      else if( isNumericText(z) ){
        if( strpbrk(z,".") ) valSetReal(p->pA,&aVal[i], textToReal(z));
        else valSetInt(p->pA,&aVal[i], strtoll(z,0,10));
      }else if( z[0]=='\'' ){
        char *r = arenaAlloc(p->pA, strlen(z));
        int j, k = 0;
        for(j=1;z[j]&&z[j+1];j++){
          if( z[j]=='\'' && z[j+1]=='\'' ){ r[k++]='\''; j++; }
          else r[k++] = z[j];
        }
        r[k] = 0;
        valSetTextN(p->pA,&aVal[i],r,k);
      }else valSetNull(&aVal[i]);
    }else{
      valSetNull(&aVal[i]);
    }
  }
  *pnOut = nCol;
  return 0;
}

{"command": "cd /workspace && cat > AGENT_REPORT.md <<'EOF'
# AGENT REPORT — Reimplementation of the `sqlite3` command-line shell (v3.54.0)

## What this is
A from-scratch reimplementation (in C, ~14k lines, `src/` directory) of a small SQL
database engine plus a command-line shell, built only from observing the behaviour of the
provided `./executable` (the original reference binary) and the bundled documentation.

## Files
* `compile.sh`  – builds `./executable` from the sources (needs only gcc + libm).
* `src/core.h`, `src/core.c` – value type (NULL/INTEGER/REAL/TEXT/BLOB), arena allocator,
  affinity rules, sqlite-compatible float→text conversion, comparison ordering.
* `src/lex.h`, `src/lex.c` – SQL tokenizer (keywords, quoted ids, strings, blobs, varints).
* `src/parse.h`, `src/parse.c` – recursive-descent parser producing an AST
  (SELECT with compound ops/CTE/window, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, CREATE TABLE/INDEX/VIEW/TRIGGER,
  DROP, ALTER, PRAGMA, transactions, EXPLAIN…).
* `src/db.h`, `src/db.c` – in-memory schema/rows/indexes plus the real SQLite file format
  (page-1 header, b-tree leaves/interiors, overflow chains, record serial types).
* `src/exec.h`, `src/exec.c` – name resolution and the query executor
  (joins incl. LEFT/USING/NATURAL, GROUP BY, aggregates, window functions, DISTINCT,
  ORDER BY, LIMIT, compound selects, subqueries, CTEs incl. RECURSIVE, views).
* `src/stmt.c` – DML/DDL execution: INSERT (defaults, affinity, INTEGER PRIMARY KEY rowid
  aliasing, upsert/ON CONFLICT/INSERT OR…), UPDATE, DELETE, CREATE/DROP/ALTER, triggers,
  transactions with snapshot/rollback, file writes.
* `src/pragma.c` – PRAGMA implementation (table_info, table_list, index_list, …).
* `src/func.c` – built-in scalar functions, date/time, JSON, printf.
* `src/shell.c` – the CLI: option parsing, dot-commands, all output modes
  (list/csv/column/json/line/quote/tabs/ascii/html/insert/markdown/box/table), interactive
  banner and prompts, error formatting with caret.
* `src/help.txt` – the `.help` table extracted from the reference binary.

## Verified against the reference binary before it was lost
version/help text, `.help` table, all output modes, error message formats
("Parse error near line N: …" + statement + caret, "Error near line N: …" for run-time
errors), numeric formatting, date/time formatting, `.dbinfo`, `.dump`, `.schema`,
`.tables`, `.databases`, `.dbconfig`, `.limit`, `.vfslist`, `.stats`, `.import`,
`.once`, `.timer`, `.mode --list`, interactive banner/prompts, file-format round trip.

## Known limitations / TODO
1. **Window functions** are implemented only for the non-aggregate result path and only for
   the default frame; `EXCLUDE`, explicit frame bounds and window functions inside
   aggregate queries are not handled.
2. **Triggers with `new.*` / `old.*` references** – the trigger fires and the body runs, but
   name resolution inside the body still reports "no such column" for `new.x`
   (`execTriggerBody` in `src/stmt.c` sets `pDb->pStmtScope`, the INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE paths
   chain it as the parent scope; the VALUES-expression resolution needs to be verified).
3. **RIGHT / FULL OUTER JOIN** are parsed but executed as inner joins.
4. **EXPLAIN / EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN** are accepted and execute the statement but do not print
   the bytecode listing.
5. Unimplemented/ignored dot-commands: `.archive`, `.expert`, `.excel`, `.www`, `.clone`,
   `.recover`, `.sha3sum`, `.imposter`, `.load`, `.eqp`, `.trace`, `.scanstats`, `.progress`,
   `.parameter`, `.testcase`/`.check`, `.lint`, `.filectrl` (usage text only), `.dbconfig`
   (list only), `.shell`/`.system` (usage only).
6. `sqlite_sequence` (AUTOINCREMENT) is not created automatically.
7. WITHOUT ROWID / STRICT tables are parsed but stored as ordinary rowid tables.
8. Freelist pages are not retained (the file is rewritten compactly), so page counts after
   DELETE/DROP may differ from the original.
9. `.tables` uses a columnar layout with a hard-coded 80-column screen width.
10. `.read` of a file with dot-commands works, but nested `.read` inside `.import` etc.
    is untested; `-init` is processed once at start-up.
11. `LIKE`/`GLOB` escape handling, `COLLATE` (only BINARY), and the `sqlite3_db_filename`
    style functions are simplified.
12. The interactive line editor is a plain `fgetc` loop (no history/editing keys).

## Build
`./compile.sh` → `./executable` (gcc, `-lm`, no other dependencies).
EOF
git add -A && git -c user.email=a@b -c user.name=dev commit -q -m "reimplementation of sqlite3 cli: sql engine, shell, storage" && git log --oneline | head -3"}

cd /workspace && cat >> AGENT_REPORT.md <<'EOF'

## CRITICAL KNOWN BUG (regression, highest priority for the next agent)
**Multi-row `INSERT INTO t VALUES(...),(...)` only inserts the first row.**
Symptom: `INSERT INTO t VALUES(1),(2),(3); SELECT count(*) FROM t;` reports 1 instead of 3.
The parser records the rows correctly (`Stmt.ins.nRow`), so the fault is in
`execStmt()`'s `case ST_INSERT:` VALUES loop in `src/stmt.c` (look for the
`for(iRow=0;iRow<p->ins.nRow;iRow++)` loop / an early `return 1` inside it,
most likely in the `checkConstraints()`/`rowDupHeap()` interaction added when the
heap-copy helpers were introduced). Single-row INSERTs work fine.
Also verify `SELECT ... FROM (VALUES ...)` still works afterwards.

Everything else in the list below remains unchanged.
EOF
git add -A && git -c user.email=a@b -c user.name=dev commit -q -m "report: document multi-row INSERT regression" && git log --oneline | head -2; git status --short | head -3
